title: Pseudo ε-Net Method with Delayed Decisions Based on Representatives and Anti-Representatives for Multi-Agent Stream Classification
content: A method for constructing a pseudo ε-net for stream classification in metric spaces is proposed, aimed at real-time multi-agent systems. The method significantly reduces the set of stored elements of the classified sequence by introducing the notions of a representative — the center of a ball with a specific action label, where all elements of the classified set correspond to that action — and an anti-representative — the center of an uncertainty ball in which no single action can be uniquely chosen. Uncertainty balls allow an agent to defer the decision on an action until the next iteration of communication with other agents. Sufficient conditions for the existence of a pseudo ε-net are formulated in terms of ε-consistency of action classes. An algorithm for constructing the pseudo ε-net is proposed, and its complexity estimates are obtained. Using a traffic balancing problem as an example, experiments show that due to more precise identification of decision confidence regions compared to known classification methods, the proposed method achieves high classification accuracy and significantly reduces the number of elements of the classified set that need to be stored; it also allows agents to terminate message exchange early without loss of balancing quality.
